question.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\sqrt{3}t,\,{t}^{2},\,t+1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$

current_example.problem: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t) =  \langle 1, \, \sqrt{2} t,\, -t^2 \rangle.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,\sqrt{2},\,-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a$ and $||\mathbf v||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨1,\,\sqrt{2}t,\,-{t}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,\sqrt{2},\,-2t⟩ \\  & =2t+2{t}^{3} \\  & =2t({t}^{2}+1), \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(1)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2}t)}^{2}+{(-{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}} \\  & ={t}^{2}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2t({t}^{2}+1)}{{t}^{2}+1} \\  & =2t.\end{aligned}
$$
